title: 赴英留学生的残酷现实（2）
desc: 赴英留学生的残酷现实（2）

paragraphs.en: Once students got their offers, they were passed on to the visa team, and finally delivered to universities as a fully wrapped, fee-paying package.
paragraphs.zh: 一旦学生拿到录取通知书，他们就会被移交给签证团队，最后被打包成一个完整的、会交学费的"产品"送到大学手里。

paragraphs.en: Over time, Kapoor felt worse and worse about her role in this system. "I knew if I worked on 100 applications, 98 were getting nowhere with their life," she said. "I mean, I woke up and I started lying, then I slept lying, and I woke up only to lie again."
paragraphs.zh: 随着时间的推移，卡普尔对自己在这个体系中的角色感到越来越不安。"我知道，如果我处理100份申请，其中有98个人的人生都不会有什么出路，"她说。"我是说，我醒来就开始说谎，然后带着谎言入睡，再醒来又继续说谎。"

paragraphs.en: Eventually, she quit the job. In response to these claims, a spokesperson for StudyIn said they "certainly do not reflect our ethos or operational practice", adding that the organisation "takes the integrity of student applications and the quality of advice we provide extremely seriously".
paragraphs.zh: 最终，她辞去了这份工作。针对这些说法，StudyIn的一位发言人表示，这些描述"肯定不能反映我们的理念或操作实践"，并补充说，该机构"极其严肃地对待学生申请材料的真实性和我们提供建议的质量"。

paragraphs.en: In the UK, a quarter of total university income is generated by international students, who pay much higher fees than home students. To attract them, British universities rely on vast, largely unregulated networks of agents operating primarily in Asia and Africa.
paragraphs.zh: 在英国，大学总收入的四分之一来自国际学生，他们支付的学费远高于本地学生。为了吸引这些人，英国大学依赖的是庞大且基本不受监管的中介网络，这些中介主要分布在亚洲和非洲。

paragraphs.en: "It's become a dogfight for students," said Gautham Kolluri, an education agent based in Canada. The industry, which helps students apply not just to the UK but to the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and beyond, is thriving in India. Each year more than a million students travel overseas to study.
paragraphs.zh: "争抢学生已经变成了一场混战，"驻加拿大的教育中介高瑟姆·科鲁里说。这个行业不仅帮助学生申请英国，还帮助他们申请美国、加拿大、澳大利亚、新西兰等地，在印度正蓬勃发展。每年有超过一百万名学生出国留学。

paragraphs.en: The reason British universities spend so much to attract international students is simple: if they were to rely solely on home students, they would go bust. In 2012, the coalition government slashed direct grants to universities and raised the annual cap on tuition fees to £9,000. In the intervening 14 years, fees for undergraduates from the UK have barely risen – the maximum was increased to £9,250 in 2017 and by a further £285 in 2025 – even as this sum has been drastically devalued by inflation.
paragraphs.zh: 英国大学之所以愿意花大价钱吸引国际学生，原因很简单：如果只靠本地学生，它们早就破产了。2012年，联合政府大幅削减了对大学的直接拨款，并将每年的学费上限提高到9000英镑。随后的14年里，英国本土本科生的学费几乎没有上涨——2017年最高涨到9250英镑，2025年又增加了285英镑——而与此同时，这笔钱早已被通货膨胀严重稀释。

paragraphs.en: The result has been a catastrophic funding crisis. The easiest solution has been to recruit international students, whose fees are not capped. They sometimes pay three times as much as their domestic counterparts for the same courses.
paragraphs.zh: 结果是灾难性的资金危机。最简单的解决办法就是招收国际学生，因为他们的学费没有上限。有时他们为同一门课程支付的费用是本地学生的三倍。

paragraphs.en: At the same time that universities have been pushed into recruiting more and more foreign students, successive governments have pledged to cut immigration. Caught between these contradictory forces are students such as Sam, betting everything on a system that not design to work for them.
paragraphs.zh: 就在大学被迫招收越来越多外国学生的同时，历届政府却承诺要削减移民。夹在这些矛盾力量之间的是像萨姆这样的学生，他们把一切都押在了一个本就不为他们而设的体系上。

paragraphs.en: The image many people have of an international student is a rich kid from the globe-trotting elite. In the 2000s, there was some basis for this stereotype. One person who worked for a London university during this period told me that his remit was to find "well-connected socialites" in China who could recruit other wealthy young people from their social circles. "We were looking for the kind of person for whom money is no object," he said.
paragraphs.zh: 很多人对国际学生的印象是那种出身精英家庭、满世界跑的富家子弟。在2000年代，这种刻板印象确实有点道理。当时在伦敦一所大学工作的人告诉我，他的任务就是在中国寻找"人脉广泛的社交名流"，让他们从自己的圈子里再拉来其他有钱的年轻人。"我们找的是那种花钱不眨眼的人，"他说。

paragraphs.en: Someone who worked in university recruitment from 2010 to 2018 told me she left the sector as things changed. "My first job was at a Russell Group university, where most foreign students were well-off, and it was clear that they were coming out with a solid degree," she said.
paragraphs.zh: 一位在2010年至2018年间从事大学招生工作的人告诉我，她是随着形势变化离开这个行业的。"我的第一份工作是在一所罗素集团的大学，那里的大多数外国学生家境殷实，而且很明显，他们毕业后拿到的学位含金量很高，"她说。

paragraphs.en: Later, when she moved to a postgraduate law school, her experience was different. "Many overseas students were struggling financially, getting into huge amounts of debt because they'd been told it would be easy to find a job in law afterwards. It felt morally wrong." A 2018 study by an Indian university surveyed students attending an English-language training school in the hopes of studying abroad and found that 80% came from farming families, mostly from small farms.
paragraphs.zh: 后来，她转到一所研究生法学院，情况就不同了。"很多海外学生经济上很吃力，背上了巨额债务，因为他们事先被告知以后很容易找到法律方面的工作。这让我觉得道德上有问题。"2018年，印度一所大学做了一项研究，调查了那些希望通过出国留学而上英语培训学校的学生，结果发现80%的人来自务农家庭，而且大多是小型农场。

paragraphs.en: Between 2017 and 2022, the number of new overseas entrants to UK universities almost doubled – and in 2021 an industry body estimated education agents were involved in roughly half of international admissions. Some in the sector suggest the number is likely to be even higher.
paragraphs.zh: 2017年至2022年间，英国大学的新增海外入学人数几乎翻了一番——而在2021年，一个行业机构估计，教育中介参与了大约一半的国际招生。业内有些人认为，这个比例可能还要更高。

paragraphs.en: The UK does not collect official data on education agents, but the Australian government does, and it recently found that agents were involved in almost 80% of international student admissions.
paragraphs.zh: 英国并没有收集教育中介的官方数据，但澳大利亚政府有，他们最近发现，近80%的国际学生录取都有中介的参与。

paragraphs.en: The rise of this industry has mostly happened below the radar. In India, large agencies have sprung up, striking deals with international universities – they typically receive between 15% and 30% of a student's fees – but operating through vast networks of subagents who do not always adhere to ethical standards.
paragraphs.zh: 这个行业的崛起大多是在公众视野之外发生的。在印度，大型中介机构如雨后春笋般涌现，它们与国际大学达成协议——通常会收取学生学费的15%到30%作为佣金——但它们通过庞大的下级代理网络运作，而这些下级代理并不总能遵守道德标准。

paragraphs.en: "A lot of subagents have never travelled to the country or institution they're recruiting for," said Kolluri. "Everyone just wants the money. I see it as student trafficking."
paragraphs.zh: "很多下级代理从未去过他们为之招生的国家或学校，"科鲁里说。"每个人都只想要钱。在我看来，这就像贩卖学生。"
